11	/**
12	 * Selector contract for a later step (the ZimmProductCard organism, SFCC-236 Step 6): stable
13	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
14	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.
15	 * Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too — mirrors the same contract
16	 * `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` documents for its own slots:
17	 *   - "content"   — the outermost element (this component's root).
18	 *   - "price"     — the price wrapper. Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's
19	 *                   own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover per variation (see the `showBag`/

21	 *   - "sizeChips" — the size-chip-group wrapper (present only when `showSizeChips` is true).
22	 *                   Always rendered in the DOM per Figma's `hidden=true` default on the "Size
23	 *                   Selector instance" node — the organism's hover-reveal CSS is what handles
24	 *                   visibility, not this component's own recipe (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts).

28	// reasoning zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx already documents: a router `Link` delivers "URL updates
29	// without a full page reload" for real. There is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse
30	// instead — confirmed none exists (see .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's own note on this).
31	const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);
32	
33	const messages = defineMessages({
34	  // Deliberately generic, not name-interpolated ("Add {name} to bag") — no such requirement was
35	  // given, and the visible product name already sits immediately to this button's left in the
36	  // same row, so the accessible name does not need to repeat it.
37	  addToBag: { id: 'product_card_content.bag.add_to_bag', defaultMessage: 'Add to bag' },
38	  // Figma node 40002163:41468 (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True) — an instance of the
39	  // shared CTA/Link atom (40001908:28374/40001908:28368) with its text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in
40	  // this state. Authored here in sentence case, not literal caps, matching this codebase's
41	  // pattern of keeping translatable copy normal-case and letting the textStyle's CSS apply the
42	  // visual transform (see ZimmProductName's own normal-cased stories against `productNames`'
43	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to
44	  // match (2026-09-03, theme/foundation/typography.ts), so this renders "NOTIFY ME" correctly.
45	  notifyMe: {
46	    id: 'product_card_content.notify_me.label',
47	    defaultMessage: 'Notify me',
48	  },
49	});
50	
51	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCardContent';
52	
53	/**
54	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
55	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
56	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
57	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
58	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.
59	 */
60	type ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as'];
61	
62	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
63	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
64	  name: string;
65	  /**
66	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
67	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
68	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.
69	   * Typed as `ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel` (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`) to exactly match what that atom
70	   * actually accepts — a prior sketch of this contract assumed `'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`, which is
71	   * wrong on both ends: the atom has no `'h4'` at all, and it does accept `'h1'` (unlikely in
72	   * practice for a grid card, but not this component's place to forbid what the atom allows).
73	   */
74	  headingLevel: ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel;
75	  /**
76	   * PDP destination for the product name link. Not passed through `isSafeHref` — unlike
77	   * `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmContactIconRow`'s CMS-sourced hrefs, this is an SFCC-generated product URL,
78	   * the same trust level `ZimmColourSwatch`'s own `href` prop already assumes.
79	   */
80	  href: string;
81	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
82	  currentPrice?: string;
83	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
84	  originalPrice?: string;
85	  /** Passed straight through to `ZimmProductPrice`'s own `isLoading`. */
86	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
87	
88	  /**
89	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
90	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved
91	   * boolean, never a variation name. When false the row is absent from the DOM entirely, not
92	   * merely visually hidden.
93	   */
94	  showAttributes: boolean;
95	  /**
96	   * Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. Pass the plain colour value ("Ivory", not
97	   * "Ivory,") — the component itself appends the trailing comma when rendering, matching
98	   * Figma's own text-node structure (confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446:
99	   * the colour text node's own content literally includes the trailing comma, e.g. "Lilac
100	   * Sand,", not a separate punctuation node). See the `colourWithComma` derivation below.
101	   */
102	  colour?: string;
103	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
104	  size?: string;
105	
106	  /** Renders the bag button (Figma "Icon_bag" — confirmed a bag action, not a wishlist star). */
107	  showBag: boolean;
108	  /** Disables the bag button (native `disabled`) when true. `onAddToBag` never fires in that state. */
109	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
110	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
111	
112	  /**
113	   * PLP-only size-chip picker, per the organism's config. Always rendered in the DOM whenever
114	   * true — Figma's `hidden=true` default on this slot is a hover-reveal CSS concern for the
115	   * Step 6 organism, not something this component enforces on itself. See the module docblock's
116	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
117	   */
118	  showSizeChips: boolean;
119	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
120	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
121	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
122	
123	  /**
124	   * True only when the caller has already resolved "unavailable AND a usable notify-me callback
125	   * exists" (the organism's job). This component still independently requires `onNotifyMe` to be
126	   * present before rendering anything — belt-and-braces, the same defensive shape
127	   * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onRemove` + `removeLabel` co-requirement uses.
128	   */
129	  showNotifyMe: boolean;
130	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
131	};
132	
133	/**
134	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
135	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
136	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
137	 * 40002163:37103).
138	 *
139	 * Deliberately has NO badge slot and NO remove/close button, even though the SFCC-236 AC
140	 * mentions a badge for PLP/Wishlist and this component sits right next to a wishlist card:
141	 *   - The badge slot that an earlier version of this plan placed on `ZimmProductCardMedia` was
142	 *     removed entirely (no design requires it) and was not moved here or anywhere else — a
143	 *     known, accepted gap, not something to fill by guessing a home for it.
144	 *   - The wishlist remove ('x') action lives entirely in `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close`
145	 *     overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not in this text-content component.
146	 *
147	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
148	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
149	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
150	 */
151	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
152	  name,
153	  headingLevel,
154	  href,
155	  currentPrice,
156	  originalPrice,
157	  isPriceLoading,
158	  showAttributes,
159	  colour,
160	  size,
161	  showBag,
162	  isUnavailable,
163	  onAddToBag,
164	  showSizeChips,
165	  sizeChipValues,
166	  selectedSizeChipValue,
167	  onSizeChipSelect,
168	  showNotifyMe,
169	  onNotifyMe,
170	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
171	  const intl = useIntl();
172	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
173	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
174	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
175	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
176	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
177	
178	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
179	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
180	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
181	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
182	
183	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
184	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
185	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
186	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
187	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
188	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
189	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
190	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
191	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
192	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
193	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
194	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
195	
196	  return (
197	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot="content">
198	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
199	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
200	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
201	        </ProductNameLink>
202	
203	        {showBag && (
204	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper}>
205	            <chakra.button
206	              type="button"
207	              __css={styles.bagButton}
208	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
209	              disabled={isUnavailable}
210	              onClick={() => {
211	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
212	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
213	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
214	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
215	                if (isUnavailable) return;
216	                onAddToBag?.();
217	              }}
218	            >
219	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
220	            </chakra.button>
221	          </chakra.div>
222	        )}
223	      </chakra.div>
224	
225	      {showAttributes && (
226	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
227	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
228	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
229	        </chakra.div>
230	      )}
231	
232	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot="price">
233	        <ZimmProductPrice
234	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
235	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
236	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
237	          isLive={false}
238	        />
239	      </chakra.div>
240	
241	      {showSizeChips && (
242	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot="sizeChips">
243	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
244	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
245	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
246	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
247	          />
248	        </chakra.div>
249	      )}
250	
251	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
252	        <chakra.button type="button" __css={styles.notifyMeButton} onClick={onNotifyMe}>
253	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
254	        </chakra.button>
255	      )}
256	    </chakra.div>
257	  );
258	};
259	
260	export default ZimmProductCardContent;

## The stretched-link / z-index CSS, and what was actually tested

Exact recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`, `root` part):
```ts
'[data-card-slot="content"] a::after': { content: '""', position: 'absolute', inset: 0 },
'[data-card-slot="close"]': { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 },
'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button': { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 },
'[data-card-slot="content"] button': { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 },
```
plus `root: { position: 'relative', width: '100%' }`.

What I actually verified, not just asserted:
1. **Confirmed the containing-block chain is clean** by reading `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly — no `position` is set anywhere in its `root`/`nameRow`/`nameLink`/other parts, so nothing between Content's `<a>` and this organism's `root` intercepts the `::after`'s `inset:0` resolution. (Media's own `root` is `position:relative` too, but Media is a sibling of Content, not an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it's irrelevant to that chain.)
2. **Compiled the exact selector shapes through this project's real installed Stylis (v4.2.0)** — the same engine Emotion/Chakra use at runtime — via a throwaway Node script (not committed). Output confirmed: the plain descendant selector and even a comma-joined list both scope correctly under the generated class (e.g. `.css-abc123 [data-card-slot="close"]{...}`), with no "only the first comma-branch gets scoped" bug. I still chose three separate keys over one comma-joined key for readability/testability, but this removed a real doubt I had before checking.
3. **Structural recipe tests** (`index.test.tsx`, "real recipe assertions" block) import the unmocked `zimmProductCard.css` module directly and assert the overlay carries no `zIndex` while each of the three lift selectors carries `position:'relative'`/`zIndex:1`.
4. **Interaction tests** fire real clicks on the bag button, carousel arrows, a size chip, and the remove button, each rendered together with the stretched-link markup, and assert the correct callback fires.

**Explicit limitation (stated in the test file's own docblock, not just here):** none of the above proves a real mouse click in an actual browser lands on the right element. jsdom does no layout/paint/hit-testing — `fireEvent`/`user-event` dispatch straight to the named node regardless of what a browser's stacking-order hit-test would actually resolve at that screen position. Steps 2/3 above prove the CSS text is correct; step 4 proves the callback wiring is correct. Going from there to "a real click lands correctly" is exactly what a real-browser (Playwright or manual) check is for, and this step has not done that check.

## Mobile-default-state question

I could not check Figma node `40002163:41477` (no tool access, as noted above). Reasoning I did verify from the existing codebase: the hover/touch split in this build is governed entirely by `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` (a pointer-capability query), not by a viewport-width breakpoint — this is Step 4's own established architecture (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s arrows-vs-indicator split uses the same query), not something I introduced. My recipe follows that same precedent for the price/size-selector swap. Given that, "mobile" and "desktop-with-a-mouse" are not actually the axis this hover-reveal logic cares about — a touch device simply never matches the query and permanently sees whatever state was set unconditionally (price for PLP/Wishlist, nothing for Home). This is a reasonable, consistent implementation, but I have **not verified** it against the specific Mobile Default node cited, so flag this as still open pending a Figma check by whoever has tool access.

## Two real deviations from the sketch (found while implementing, not assumed upfront)

1. **`ZimmProductCardBaseProps`/`ZimmProductCardPlpVariation`/`ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`/`ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` are now exported**, not module-private as the sketch implied. This was forced by a genuine TypeScript behavior I only found by running `tsc`: excess-property checking against a **union** type is weak — a fresh object literal with `variation: 'home'` plus an extra `onRemove` field does **not** get flagged, because `onRemove` is valid on a *different* union member (Wishlist). Proving "Home rejects `onRemove`" required assigning to the narrow intersection type directly, which needed it exported. The same export let me give the test file's `buildCardProps` helper proper overloads so call sites can add a variation-specific prop without fighting the union. Both `@ts-expect-error` cases in `index.test.tsx` are real, verified-by-`tsc` proof now (I caught and fixed one that was silently passing for the wrong reason before treating it as done).
2. **`onNotifyMe` needs no extra "aria-label-worthy context" from this organism** — `ZimmProductCardContent`'s real `notifyMeButton` renders its own visible text via its own internal `defineMessages`, no external label prop exists on its actual signature. The sketch's comment on this point doesn't match Content's real implementation; I did not invent a label prop that isn't there.
3. Minor correction: `ZimmProductCardMedia` has **no** `isUnavailable` prop at all (only `ZimmProductCardContent` does) — "both already handle isUnavailable generically" in the brief is imprecise; I pass `isUnavailable` only to Content.
4. **No `priority` passthrough** for Media's LCP eager-load escape hatch — not in the given contract, flagged in the file's own docblock as a known gap rather than added silently.
5. **`onNotifyMe`/`showNotifyMe` is computed uniformly across all three variations** (`Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe)`), not restricted to `plp` — this is an interpretation call given real ambiguity (the AC/Figma only confirm this for PLP, but `onNotifyMe` sits on the shared base type, and Content already supports it generically for any caller with no variation awareness).
